column1: # example-gold.tsv — a known-answer set for `nova-memory eval`, over the
# fixture corpus in testdata/corpus. It is an EXAMPLE OF THE FORM, not a
# benchmark: six rows over six files proves the harness runs and can fail,
# and proves nothing whatever about retrieval quality on your corpus.
# Format: query<TAB>expected-path-substring[,substring...]
# Blank lines and lines beginning with # are ignored. A row passes when ANY
# of its expected substrings appears in the path of some hit within top-k, so
# a lesson with more than one legitimate home lists them all. A row with no
# expectation is refused, not skipped: a case that can never hit would drag
# the measured recall down invisibly.
# GROW YOUR OWN FROM YOUR OWN RECORD. The rows that are worth having are the
# ones your record already argued about: pairs you discovered were duplicates
# after the fact, paraphrases you nearly banked twice, the question you asked
# three months apart and answered differently. Write the query the way you
# would actually ask it, not the way the file is worded — a gold set built by
# copying sentences out of the target file measures nothing but string
# equality. Add a row every time retrieval misses something you knew was
# there, and never delete a row because it fails.
how often should the lantern glazing be washed
why keep the brass polish away from the optical glass
when can the relief boat land at the jetty steps
how late is the jetty against the published tide prediction
how long does the compressor take to reach working pressure
what does a short blast mean about the drive belt
# A row may name more than one legitimate home. This one is answered by the
# distilled note AND recorded in the dated log, and either is a correct
# retrieval — which is also the reason every receipt carries its class: the
# two answers mean different things when the verdict is "have I banked this
# already?"
washing the glazing before an onshore gale
